script_execution_model.conclusion: Scripts are external Lua 5.4 source files loaded and run by the host application. They execute as ordinary blocking Lua code; there is no coroutine scheduler and no bytecode-only path. All timing is achieved by a native sleep that blocks the calling thread.

sleep_semantics.conclusion: input.sleep(ms) / input.delay(ms) call a host function (0x693fe0) that calls the imported Windows Sleep directly. enableDebug wraps it with two extra toggles.
disassembly_0x693fe0: push ebp; mov ebp,esp; push esi; mov esi,[ebp+8]
test esi,esi; jns 0x693ff4; mov eax,esi; cdq; mov esi,eax; xor esi,edx; sub esi,edx   ; abs(ms)
push 1; call dword ptr [0xa3dc00]    ; debug toggle A
push esi; call dword ptr [0xa3d554]  ; Sleep(ms)
push 1; call dword ptr [0xa3dc04]    ; debug toggle B
0x694018: push esi; call dword ptr [0xa3d554]; ret
sleep_semantics.implication: A Lua script that calls sleep(1000) in a loop blocks its own thread for real wall-clock time. Route progress and stuck detection therefore advance concurrently on other host threads, which is why the sample polls mi_isRunning()/mi_getPos() instead of driving movement itself.

lua_module_registration.conclusion: Lua C functions are registered per-module by a stack-local table of {name-address, function-address} pairs that is walked with lua_pushcclosure + lua_setfield. This mechanism is fully recovered for the 'input' module (50 entries).

register_function.signature: int luaopen_input_module(lua_State* L)  // lua_CFunction: L at [ebp+8], returns 1
structure: prologue: push ebp / mov ebp,esp / sub esp,0x198
body: mov dword ptr [ebp-0x198], <nameVA> ; mov dword ptr [ebp-0x194], <funcVA> ; ... 8-byte stride
0x4e51b0: load next name; test esi,esi; jne 0x4e5194 ; loop until null name
epilogue: mov eax,1 ; mov esp,ebp ; pop ebp ; ret

mi_module_status.inference: The mi_* bindings are most likely installed by a registration routine whose table lives in a VMProtect-virtualized region or is constructed at runtime, and/or the names at 0xa48504+ are the error-report argument strings ('%s[%d]: %s' at 0xa48a0c) for the mi_ implementations rather than a literal luaL_Reg table.
mi_module_status.impact: Does not change the execution model. It only leaves the exact Lua-binding call site unnamed.

file_access.question: Does ZeusTool read the game's files?
file_access.conclusion: No evidence of reading the game's Unity asset files. It reads its own config/data/script files, and obtains game state through shared memory rather than from game files.

recorder_dsl_layer.conclusion: The main EXE embeds a complete intermediate-representation layer for the recorder's compressed notation (_MLD{}/_MDLY{}/func-end), including code generation back into executable script text. This is a THIRD linguistic layer, below the Lua layer.
semantics: A recorded timeline is normalised into <--TOKEN--value--> markers (regex substitution), then regenerated as _MDLY{delta} + _TOKEN{n} text: absolute timing is rebuilt as a delay followed by the action, and {1} is a 1-tick hold rather than a 1 ms hold.
The generator also emits real script structure: 'func <Name>()' bodies, 'end', and wrapper functions that invoke another function as a macro (_PassEB8DA04CC7{99999}).

The same compressed notation survives into hand-edited shared libraries (研究/公用指令集.txt uses func/end plus _MLD{10}_MLU{400}E{500} and _来回走{99999}), which is why the notation had to be understood by the client too.
Not resolved: which character class each of the 2/4/6/X regexes selects. The digit discriminating among four regexes is confirmed as data, but its meaning (key-class vs variant) is not established.

cross_layer_model.control_flow: Lua script thread: mi_* -> host state/route structures -> native runtime loop thread (coordinate feedback, 50-unit arrival test) -> 0x78-byte command block in mapped memory -> plugin64.dll in game process -> hooked input readers / Mono calls
